sketches: (even hole, K4)-free graphs form a subclass of even-hole-free graphs, so resolving MIS on even-hole-free graphs (positively) settles the (even hole, K4)-free half of 2001.01607__03; the (theta, triangle)-free half is separate (thetas contain even holes, but triangle-freeness is an extra restriction).

source.name: MIS complexity in even-hole-free graphs
source.statement: The complexity of computing a maximum independent set in an even-hole-free graph is not known.
source.context: Stated in the introduction as motivation for the paper's approach. The paper proves a polynomial-time algorithm for the strictly smaller class of (even hole, pyramid)-free graphs, with the hope that understanding the pyramid-free case may shed light on the full even-hole-free class.

target.name: MIS complexity for (even hole, K₄)-free graphs
target.statement: Determine the computational complexity of the Maximum Independent Set problem for (even hole, $K_4$)-free graphs and for (theta, triangle)-free graphs.
target.context: Maximum Independent Set is polynomial for (even hole, triangle)-free and (even hole, pyramid)-free graphs. The paper gives polynomial algorithms for (theta, triangle, $S_{i,j,k}$)-free and (even hole, pyramid, $K_t$, $S_{i,j,k}$)-free graphs via bounded treewidth, but the complexity for the larger classes (even hole, $K_4$)-free and (theta, triangle)-free is stated as unknown.

sketches: The conjectured dichotomy places every spider S_{i,j,k} on the polynomial side, so it would determine (as P) the complexity of MIS on S_{i,j,k}-free graphs for the cases containing P7, S_{1,1,3}, S_{1,2,2} asked in 2001.01607__04.

source.name: MIS dichotomy for path- and claw-subdivision-free graphs
source.statement: For every connected graph $H$, Maximum Independent Set in $H$-free graphs is in $\mathsf{P}$ if and only if $H \in \{P_\ell\}_{\ell} \cup \{S_{i,j,k}\}_{i \leq j \leq k}$.
source.context: The polynomial-time complexity of MIS in $H$-free graphs has been studied since the early 1980s. Alekseev showed that if $H$ is neither a path nor a subdivided claw then MIS is NP-complete on $H$-free graphs, motivating this conjecture about the full dichotomy. The authors note that an even stronger conjecture is postulated by Lozin [28].

target.name: MIS complexity for S_{i,j,k}-free graphs with P₇
target.statement: Determine the computational complexity of the Maximum Independent Set problem for $H$-free graphs whenever $H$ is some $S_{i,j,k}$ that contains either $P_7$, $S_{1,1,3}$, or $S_{1,2,2}$.
target.context: The problem is polynomial for $H \subseteq P_k$ with $k \leq 6$ and for $H \subseteq S_{i,j,k}$ with $(i,j,k) \leq (1,1,2)$, and is NP-hard when $H$ is not an induced subgraph of any $S_{i,j,k}$. The boundary region where $H$ contains $P_7$, $S_{1,1,3}$, or $S_{1,2,2}$ is listed as completely open.

sketches: O_k-free graphs have induced cycle packing number < k, hence induced odd cycle packing number iocp < k (odd cycles are cycles). So tractability of MIS on bounded-iocp graphs implies polynomial MIS on O_k-free graphs for each fixed k.

source.name: MIS tractability in bounded-iocp graphs
source.statement: Maximum Independent Set could be tractable in graphs with bounded $\mathrm{iocp}$ (induced odd cycle packing number).
source.context: The paper establishes tractability of MIS for graphs with bounded induced cycle packing number ($\mathrm{icp}$, i.e., $\mathcal{O}_k$-free graphs) in the sparse case, and quasipolynomial time in general. The authors remark that extending this to bounded $\mathrm{iocp}$ would be a surprising and formidable generalisation of Conjecture 1.3 and of the known polynomial-time result for bounded $\mathrm{ocp}$ (odd cycle packing number).

target.name: Polynomial MIS in 𝒪_k-free graphs
target.statement: Maximum Independent Set is solvable in polynomial time in $\mathcal{O}_{k}$-free graphs.
target.context: The paper proves that sparse $\mathcal{O}_k$-free graphs have logarithmic treewidth, making Maximum Independent Set polynomial in the sparse case (Corollary 1.2). A quasipolynomial algorithm is also given for general $\mathcal{O}_k$-free graphs, stopping just short of resolving this conjecture in full generality.

sketches: The bounded sub-determinant IP conjecture explicitly yields (its 'in particular' clause) polynomial stable set for all graphs with ocp(G) <= k; restricting to graphs embedded in a surface of arbitrary Euler genus gives 1908.06300__01 by hypothesis-class containment.
The source explicitly asserts stable set is polynomial for every fixed ocp(G) <= k on all graphs, which contains the subclass of graphs embedded in a surface of arbitrary Euler genus.

source.name: Polynomial-time bounded sub-determinant integer programs
source.statement: Integer programs with bounded sub-determinants can be solved in polynomial time. In particular, the stable set problem on graphs with $\mathrm{ocp}(G) \leq k$ is polynomial for every fixed $k$.
source.context: The authors note that recent work links the complexity of integer programs to the magnitude of their sub-determinants, and that it is tempting to believe bounded sub-determinant integer programs are polynomial-time solvable. This would imply the stable set problem is polynomial for every fixed bound $k$ on the odd cycle packing number, which remains open for $k \geq 2$.

target.name: Stable set for bounded ocp, unbounded genus
target.statement: Is the stable set problem polynomial-time solvable for graphs $G$ with $\mathrm{ocp}(G) \leq k$ (for fixed $k$) embedded in a surface of arbitrary Euler genus?
target.context: The paper's main result (Theorem 2) gives a polynomial-time algorithm when both the odd cycle packing number and the Euler genus are fixed constants. Immediately after stating this result the authors note they do not know whether the genus bound can be dropped while retaining polynomial-time solvability.
